text:
The United Kingdom joins Canada and more countries at SAF Global Summit 2026 in London, where global aviation leaders will tackle sustainable fuel, investment, policy and aviation’s future.

The United Kingdom joins Canada and more countries at SAF Global Summit 2026, bringing global aviation leaders together in London on 22 and 23 September. The high-profile event comes as airlines, governments and fuel producers face mounting pressure to cut aviation emissions. Meanwhile, sustainable aviation fuel is moving rapidly from long-term ambition to an immediate industry priority.

The summit will therefore examine policy, investment, production, infrastructure and demand. In addition, senior representatives from aviation, energy and government will debate how the sector can expand SAF supply. As a result, the London gathering could offer important signals about aviation’s next major fuel transition.

The SAF Global Summit 2026 will bring airlines, governments, fuel producers, airports, investors and technology companies together in London on 22 and 23 September, as the aviation industry faces growing pressure to turn sustainable aviation fuel ambitions into commercially viable supply.

Hosted at the QEII Centre, the two-day event is expected to focus on one of aviation’s biggest challenges: how to increase SAF production, secure investment and build the infrastructure needed to get more sustainable fuel into aircraft.

With governments introducing mandates and airlines announcing increasingly ambitious decarbonisation strategies, the summit comes at an important moment for the global aviation industry.

London becomes a meeting point for the SAF industry

SAF has moved from being a niche sustainability discussion to a strategic issue for airlines, airports and governments.

Unlike conventional jet fuel, sustainable aviation fuel can be produced from a range of renewable and waste-based feedstocks, depending on the technology and pathway used. It can also be blended with conventional aviation fuel and used in existing aircraft within current technical limits.

However, the industry’s challenge is no longer simply proving that SAF can work. The bigger question is whether production can increase quickly enough, while keeping costs manageable and creating a reliable supply chain.

That question will be central to the SAF Global Summit 2026, which is being positioned around policy, investment, production, supply chains and innovation.

The organiser expects more than 1,000 attendees, with more than 150 speakers and participation from senior decision-makers across aviation, energy, government and finance.

Policy pressure is changing the aviation fuel market

Government policy is becoming one of the strongest drivers of SAF demand.

Europe, the UK and other major aviation markets are introducing regulatory mechanisms designed to increase the use of sustainable fuels. These measures are intended to create demand and provide producers with greater certainty when making large-scale investment decisions.

The summit is therefore expected to examine how different policy frameworks are shaping the market and whether regulation can provide the stability required for SAF projects to reach commercial scale.

Among the frameworks likely to attract attention are the ReFuelEU Aviation regulation, the UK SAF Mandate and policy incentives in the United States.

For airlines, the implications are significant. SAF is generally more expensive than conventional jet fuel, meaning that increased regulatory requirements could affect operating costs, ticket economics and procurement strategies.

For producers and investors, however, long-term demand created by mandates can make new projects more attractive.

The industry’s challenge is finding a balance between environmental ambition, affordability and sufficient investment.

Countries represented at SAF Global Summit 2026

Airlines look beyond announcements to actual supply

Airlines have increasingly committed to reducing their carbon footprint, but achieving those goals depends heavily on access to lower-carbon fuels.

The summit will examine how voluntary airline demand, corporate purchasing and regulatory obligations can translate into long-term SAF offtake agreements.

Representatives from major aviation groups are expected to discuss the relationship between airline demand and investment in production capacity.

This is particularly important because announcing an SAF target does not automatically create fuel supply.

Producers need confidence that airlines and other customers will purchase the fuel. Airlines, meanwhile, need confidence that sufficient volumes will be available at commercially acceptable prices.

Long-term offtake agreements can help bridge that gap by giving SAF developers greater visibility over future revenues while allowing airlines to secure part of their future fuel requirements.

Investment could determine how quickly SAF scales

The financing of SAF production is another major theme at the London gathering.

Building commercial-scale SAF facilities requires substantial capital, while projects can face uncertainty around technology, feedstock availability, energy prices, regulation and future demand.

Investors therefore need projects that are technically credible and commercially bankable.

The summit is expected to examine how SAF projects can move towards final investment decisions and what producers require from airlines, governments and financial institutions.

Different SAF pathways will also remain part of the conversation.

These include fuels produced from waste oils and other feedstocks, as well as emerging power-to-liquid or synthetic fuel technologies. Each pathway has different requirements, costs, scalability questions and sustainability considerations.

The result is an industry that cannot rely on a single technology to solve aviation’s fuel challenge.

Airports face the last-mile challenge

Increasing SAF production is only one part of the equation.

The fuel must eventually reach airports, be stored and blended where required, and then delivered efficiently to aircraft.

That makes airport infrastructure and fuel logistics an increasingly important part of the SAF discussion.

The summit’s programme includes a session focused on what it describes as bridging the “last-mile to wing-tip”. The discussion is expected to bring airlines, airports and fuel suppliers together to consider how financial certainty, airport preparedness and logistics coordination can improve SAF availability.

This issue has direct implications for the wider travel industry.

Even if production increases, inconsistent availability at airports could make it harder for airlines to incorporate SAF into routine operations. A more coordinated supply network could therefore become as important as additional production capacity.

Technology remains critical to the next phase

SAF development is also closely connected to innovation.

The industry is exploring multiple production routes, feedstocks and technologies, while researchers and companies continue to work on improving yields, reducing costs and increasing the environmental benefits of alternative aviation fuels.

Technology alone, however, cannot deliver the transition.

A viable SAF market needs a combination of technology, capital, policy, feedstock, infrastructure and committed buyers.

That interconnected nature of the challenge is one reason events such as the SAF Global Summit have become increasingly relevant to aviation executives.

A broader commercial market is emerging

The 2026 event will also feature a SAF Market & Trade Forum, bringing together senior representatives from the investment, buying, trading and production sides of the industry.

The forum is expected to focus on the development of a more mature SAF market, including investment structures, demand signals and trading mechanisms.

This reflects a broader change in the sector.

SAF is increasingly being treated not simply as an environmental product, but as a strategic commodity that will require established procurement, financing and trading systems if it is to reach global scale.

Why the summit matters for travellers

Most passengers will never see the SAF supply chain directly. Yet the decisions made by governments, airlines, fuel companies and investors could eventually affect the cost and sustainability of air travel.

If SAF production expands successfully, airlines could gain access to larger volumes of lower-carbon fuel. If costs remain high or supply growth falls short, the transition could prove slower and more expensive.

The SAF Global Summit 2026 in London therefore arrives at a critical point for aviation.

The industry already has ambitious climate targets. The next test is implementation.

Over two days at the QEII Centre, the focus will be on whether policy can attract investment, whether investment can unlock production, whether production can reach airports and whether airlines can turn commitments into sustained demand.

For global aviation, that chain of decisions could determine how quickly SAF moves from an emerging alternative into an increasingly important part of the industry’s future fuel mix.

The cause is clear: aviation needs to reduce carbon emissions while global air travel continues to grow. However, limited SAF production, high costs and complex supply chains remain major barriers. The answer is stronger cooperation between governments, airlines, fuel producers, airports, investors and technology companies. SAF Global Summit 2026 provides a platform for that cooperation. The reason the United Kingdom, Canada and more countries are participating is that no single aviation market can build a global SAF economy alone. Therefore, international policy alignment, investment and reliable fuel supply will be essential. The summit will explore how these challenges can become practical opportunities.

The United Kingdom, Canada and more countries are converging at SAF Global Summit 2026 as the aviation industry enters a decisive period for sustainable fuel. The event is bringing global aviation leaders together in London to examine what must happen beyond ambitious climate pledges. Crucially, the discussion will focus on turning policy into investment, investment into production and production into dependable airport supply.

Airlines need access to SAF. Producers need long-term demand. Investors need commercially credible projects. Governments need effective policies. Therefore, cooperation across borders will be central to the industry’s progress. The summit also gives aviation executives an opportunity to assess emerging technologies, feedstock availability, infrastructure requirements and market mechanisms. Ultimately, the United Kingdom’s participation alongside Canada and other international markets highlights the increasingly global nature of the SAF challenge. What happens next could influence how quickly sustainable aviation fuel becomes a larger part of commercial air travel.

text:
New Delhi: An Air India pilot died during a layover at a hotel in Delhi, with police ruling out foul play while awaiting the final medical opinion on the cause of death.

The pilot, Captain Sunny Sharad Asaldekar, 46, was found unconscious and unresponsive in his room at The Grand hotel in Vasant Kunj on the evening of September 11. He had checked into the hotel on September 10 while in Delhi for Boeing 787 conversion training. Asaldekar had previously worked with Air India Express before moving to Air India.

According to police, Asaldekar’s brother became concerned after being unable to reach him by phone and contacted the hotel management. The hotel manager went to the room and found the door locked from inside. After receiving no response, the room was opened using a master key, and the pilot was found lying unconscious. He was taken to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

Initial reports attributed the death to a suspected cardiac arrest, but police have said that the exact cause has not yet been conclusively established. A post-mortem examination was conducted at Safdarjung Hospital on September 12, and the final medical opinion is awaited. Police have initiated inquest proceedings under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

Police have ruled out foul play based on their preliminary investigation, while continuing to examine the circumstances surrounding the death. A crime team also inspected the hotel room as part of the investigation.

Air India expressed deep sadness over the death of its cockpit crew member and said it was in contact with the pilot’s family and would provide all necessary support. Reports said Asaldekar was undergoing conversion training to operate the Boeing 787 and was expected to undertake flight duties following the training.

title: Kades, Perpanjangan Jabatan, dan Bayang-Bayang Kepentingan 2029! - LINTASTUNGKAL
description:
Ketika dalih efisiensi anggaran bertemu dengan kepentingan politik, publik berhak bertanya: ini soal desa atau soal kekuasaan?
Pilkades membutuhkan biaya.
Tetapi efisiensi tidak boleh menjadi kata sakti yang otomatis membenarkan perpanjangan kekuasaan.
Kalau persoalannya benar-benar anggaran, publik layak melihat perhitungannya secara terbuka.
Dan kekuasaan membutuhkan batas.
text:
Ketika dalih efisiensi anggaran bertemu dengan kepentingan politik, publik berhak bertanya: ini soal desa atau soal kekuasaan?

Wacana memperpanjang masa jabatan kepala desa kembali masuk ke ruang publik.

Pada Rabu, 9 September 2026, puluhan ribu kepala desa yang tergabung dalam Kepala Desa Akhir Masa Jabatan (AMJ) 2027–2029 menyampaikan aspirasi kepada DPR RI. Mereka meminta agar masa jabatan kepala desa yang akan berakhir pada periode tersebut dapat diperpanjang.

Menyampaikan aspirasi tentu merupakan hak demokratis.

Tetapi ada hal lain yang juga menjadi hak publik: mempertanyakan alasan, timing, serta dampak politik dari sebuah kebijakan.

Dan di sinilah persoalannya mulai menarik.

Wacana tersebut muncul ketika Indonesia perlahan memasuki fase menuju Pemilu 2029. Ribuan kepala desa yang tersebar di seluruh Indonesia bukan sekadar pejabat administratif. Mereka berada sangat dekat dengan masyarakat—mengenal tokoh lokal, kelompok masyarakat, jaringan sosial, hingga dinamika politik di tingkat akar rumput.

Maka pertanyaan publik sebenarnya sederhana:

Mengapa perpanjangan masa jabatan kembali didorong sekarang?

DALIH EFISIENSI ATAU KENYAMANAN KEKUASAAN?

Argumen mengenai efisiensi anggaran tidak bisa langsung ditolak.

Pilkades membutuhkan biaya. Ada anggaran penyelenggaraan, administrasi, pengamanan, logistik, serta berbagai kebutuhan lain yang harus dipersiapkan pemerintah daerah.

Menunda atau mengatur kembali pelaksanaan Pilkades memang berpotensi menghasilkan efisiensi.

Tetapi efisiensi tidak boleh menjadi kata sakti yang otomatis membenarkan perpanjangan kekuasaan.

Kalau persoalannya benar-benar anggaran, publik layak melihat perhitungannya secara terbuka.

Berapa biaya Pilkades yang dapat dihemat?

Berapa biaya pemerintahan yang muncul akibat perpanjangan?

Berapa desa yang terdampak?

Dan apakah ada alternatif lain yang lebih efisien tanpa harus memperpanjang masa jabatan kepala desa yang sedang berkuasa?

Pertanyaan itu penting.

Sebab kebijakan publik seharusnya berdiri di atas data, bukan hanya narasi.

UU SUDAH MENENTUKAN: 8 TAHUN

Ada persoalan hukum yang juga tidak boleh dilewati.

Melalui UU Nomor 3 Tahun 2024 tentang Perubahan Kedua atas UU Nomor 6 Tahun 2014 tentang Desa, masa jabatan kepala desa ditetapkan selama delapan tahun dan dapat menjabat paling banyak dua kali masa jabatan.

Aturan tersebut masih relatif baru.

Karena itu, ketika kembali muncul gagasan memperpanjang masa jabatan, publik wajar meminta penjelasan:

Apa persoalan mendasar yang membuat aturan yang baru diubah tersebut kembali perlu diubah?

Jangan sampai undang-undang diperlakukan seperti papan tulis yang bisa dihapus dan ditulis ulang setiap kali kebutuhan kekuasaan berubah.

Hukum membutuhkan kepastian.

Demokrasi membutuhkan regenerasi.

Dan kekuasaan membutuhkan batas.

text:
Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre & Hyderabad International Convention Centre (HICC) has announced the elevation of Shyama Maity to Director of Rooms, recognising her contribution to the property since joining the hotel in 2024 and her strong track record in driving guest experience, operational excellence and Rooms Division performance.

Shyama brings close to 20 years of international hospitality experience spanning Rooms Division operations, Front Office, Housekeeping, Guest Relations, Concierge and Reservations. During her tenure at Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre & HICC, she progressed from Rooms Division Manager to Director of Rooms, taking on increasing responsibility for one of the hotel’s most critical operational functions.

New responsibilities

In her new role, Shyama will lead the hotel’s Rooms Division, overseeing Front Office, Housekeeping, Guest Relations, Concierge and Reservations across the property’s 287 rooms. Her mandate will encompass guest experience, service delivery, Rooms revenue, occupancy, ADR and RevPAR, alongside quality, brand and sustainability standards. She will also continue to play a key role in people development, operational planning and delivering seamless experiences for large-scale MICE movements, corporate groups and high-profile stays.

Role across MICE, weddings and leisure

Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre is also a destination for weddings and social celebrations. Its event offering brings together accommodation, dining, banqueting and recreation, making the Rooms Division an important part of the overall event experience, from welcoming wedding guests and families to managing group arrivals and ensuring seamless stays for MICE delegates.

With the property balancing high-volume conventions and corporate movements with weddings, social celebrations and leisure stays, the Rooms Division plays a pivotal role in connecting every part of the guest journey. From pre-arrival planning and room readiness to personalised service, guest recovery and departure, the team ensures that the experience remains consistent across every segment.

Leadership perspective

Commenting on the elevation, Rubin Cherian, General Manager, Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre & HICC, said,“Shyama’s elevation is a reflection of the leadership, commitment and operational depth she has demonstrated during her time with us. Since joining Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre & HICC, she has made a meaningful impact across the Rooms Division, with a clear focus on guest experience, people development and business performance. Our property operates across a unique mix of MICE, corporate, weddings and leisure, and the Rooms Division sits at the centre of each of these experiences. Shyama understands this complexity exceptionally well, and I am confident that in her new role she will continue to strengthen our Rooms operations while creating memorable experiences for every guest who walks through our doors.”

Speaking on her elevation, Shyama Maity, Director of Rooms, Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre & HICC, said,“I am honoured to take on the role of Director of Rooms at Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre & HICC. Having been part of this property since 2024, this elevation is especially meaningful to me. What makes this hotel unique is the diversity of experiences we deliver; from large-scale conventions and corporate events at HICC to weddings, social celebrations and leisure stays. Every guest has a different reason for being here, but the expectation for warm, seamless and consistent hospitality remains the same. I look forward to working closely with our teams to further strengthen our Rooms Division, develop our people and ensure that every stay reflects the service excellence that Novotel Hyderabad Convention Centre & HICC stands for.”

Career experience

Shyama’s career includes senior Rooms and Front Office leadership roles across India and New Zealand. Prior to returning to India, she served as Rooms Division Manager at Rydges Latimer Christchurch and held Front Office leadership positions at The George Christchurch. Earlier in her career, she worked with Hyatt Ahmedabad, Grand Hyatt Goa and Hyatt Regency Kolkata, including as part of the pre-opening team at Grand Hyatt Goa.

Euromääräisiä arvioita kustannusten noususta on aiempaa vaikeampi tehdä, koska epävakaaseen maailmantilanteeseen ja uusiutuvaan lentopolttoaineeseen liittyviä epävarmuuksia on useita.

text:
The BRICS Business Council and Women’s Business Alliance submitted their respective 2026 annual reports for consideration by BRICS leaders during the closing ceremony of the 18th BRICS Summit under India’s chairmanship. The reports outlined key areas for strengthening economic cooperation, supporting businesses and expanding opportunities for women-led enterprises across BRICS economies.

Business Council Focuses on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, Sustainability

The BRICS Business Council’s annual report focused on four key pillars of India’s BRICS chairmanship: resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. It highlighted the need to make better use of the collective strengths of BRICS economies in food, energy, fertilisers, manufacturing, technology, capital, natural resources and skilled talent by increasing trade and investment and developing stronger value chains.

On resilience, the report proposed a BRICS supply chain resilience framework aimed at improving information sharing and preparedness during disruptions. It also called for pilot value chains in sectors where BRICS economies can complement each other.

On innovation, the council emphasised greater cooperation in artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure and advanced manufacturing, along with stronger links between businesses, technology providers and innovation ecosystems.

The cooperation agenda focused on making cross-border business easier through paperless trade, electronic documentation and greater interoperability of digital systems.

On sustainability, the report identified areas including green hydrogen, biofuels, sustainable aviation fuel and low-carbon fuels, supported by advances in technology, standards, infrastructure and financing.

The council said the success of its recommendations would ultimately be measured through tangible outcomes such as projects launched, partnerships formed, technologies developed, and trade and investment generated.

Women’s Business Alliance Targets Scale for Women Entrepreneurs

The Women’s Business Alliance’s 2026 annual report focused on strengthening the participation and leadership of women entrepreneurs across BRICS. It identified access to markets, finance, technology, skills, business networks, value chains and procurement opportunities as important conditions for expanding women-led enterprises.

The report also stressed greater access to capital and innovation, including stronger connections between women entrepreneurs and investors and financing mechanisms that can help businesses scale. It highlighted the potential of digital public infrastructure, including UPI, to support women’s economic development and financial inclusion.

Another focus is building resilience through women-led solutions in areas such as healthcare, agriculture, food security, tourism and the creative economy. The recommendations included preventive and digital healthcare, climate-smart agriculture, intellectual property ownership and wider markets for women creators and entrepreneurs.

The alliance also called for successful practices across BRICS countries to be identified, adapted and scaled. Its knowledge reports contain 10 key recommendations covering healthcare, the inclusive economy, agriculture, the creative economy, innovative development and tourism.

The report placed scaling women-led enterprises, access to capital, innovation and market opportunities at the centre of the next phase of BRICS women’s economic cooperation.

title: Brics business council pushes supply-chain resilience, AI cooperation - TradingView

India is hosting the Brics Business Forum and the leaders' summit from 11-13 September.

Shroff submitted the 2026 annual reports of the Brics Business Council to the Brics leaders for their consideration.
India's chairmanship has been guided by the 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.
text:
New Delhi, Sept. 13 -- The Brics Business Council has called for a supply-chain resilience framework and deeper cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI), digital infrastructure and advanced manufacturing, as the grouping seeks to turn its combined economic capabilities into greater trade, investment and technology links.

The recommendations, presented during India's Brics chairmanship, span four pillars-resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability-and seek to move the grouping from broad areas of alignment towards practical business opportunities.

Speaking at the Brics session on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability on Sunday, Jai Shroff, chair, Brics Business Council and chairman and group chief executive, UPL Ltd, said the recommendations were intended as a guide for the four pillars of India's chairmanship.

"The council proposes a supply chain resilience framework for Brics to strengthen information sharing and preparedness during the disruption," Shroff said, while also pointing to the scope for pilot value chains in select sectors based on the complementary strengths of member economies

Shroff said Brics brought together significant economic capabilities across food, fuel, fertilizer, manufacturing, technology, capital, natural resources and talent. The opportunity, he said, was to connect these capabilities more effectively through greater intra-Brics trade and investment, stronger value chains, technology sharing and new business partnerships.

The resilience pillar also covers dependable supply chains, food and energy security, modern infrastructure and diversified production networks, particularly in the context of disruptions in recent years.

Innovation is the council's second focus. Technology, Shroff said, was transforming every part of the economy, from farms and factories to finance, logistics and energy. The ambition should not be limited to adopting new technologies but should also involve innovating together.

The report calls for deeper cooperation in artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure and advanced manufacturing, besides connecting business technology providers and innovation ecosystems across Brics, he said.

India is hosting the Brics Business Forum and the leaders' summit from 11-13 September.

The cooperation pillar focuses on making it easier for companies to trade, invest and operate across markets. The report therefore emphasises paperless trade, electronic documentation and greater interoperability among digital systems.

The fourth pillar, sustainability, focuses on cooperation in green hydrogen, biofuels, sustainable aviation fuel and low-carbon fuels.

"Such cooperation must be supported by progress in technology standards, infrastructure and financing. It can create new industries, value chains, investments and employment across our economies," Shroff said.

He said Brics already had enormous economic capacity, but the task was to translate that capacity into opportunities.

"For the business council's success ultimately is measured by not the number of recommendations we make but by the outcome of them. Projects launched, partnerships formed, technologies developed and trade and investment generated."

He added that governments create an enabling environment, while businesses must convert it into opportunity and economic value.

"Resilience gives our economy strength. Innovation gives us competitiveness. Cooperation gives them scale. Sustainability gives them longevity. The opportunity before us is to bring all four together," Shroff said.

The Brics Business Council, he said, was ready to work with governments and institutions to take forward the recommendations.

Shroff submitted the 2026 annual reports of the Brics Business Council to the Brics leaders for their consideration.

"We can identify areas where there is a clear business case for cooperation and make it easier for our companies to work together. India's chairmanship has been guided by the 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'. These are broad ideas for business. They are actually quite practical," he noted. text:
The Indian sugar industry needs to move beyond conventional sugar and ethanol production and evolve into integrated biorefineries that maximise value from sugarcane and its by-products, policymakers and industry leaders said at the India Sugar & Bio-Energy Conference (ISBC) 2026.

The two-day conference, organised by the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) in New Delhi on September 9-10, brought together more than 500 delegates and over 50 global speakers from India, Thailand, Brazil, Europe and the United States.

Tarun Kapoor, Advisor to the Prime Minister, said sugar mills should increasingly be viewed as integrated bio-refineries rather than standalone sugar and ethanol production units. He emphasised the need to maximise economic value from sugarcane and its various co-products and by-products.

Santosh Kumar Sarangi, Secretary, Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, said the industry had evolved from traditional sugar production towards integrated biorefineries capable of generating value from multiple streams of the sugarcane value chain.

The conference focused on the expanding role of the sugar sector in India's energy security, ethanol blending, clean mobility, circular manufacturing and sustainable industrial growth. Ashwini Srivastava, Joint Secretary, Department of Food and Public Distribution, said the future performance of sugar mills should be assessed not merely by sugar output but by their efficiency in using cane and generating value from by-products, including the value reaching the rural economy.

Discussions covered the global sugar outlook, India's 2026/27 crop and trade prospects, clean mobility and the transition in liquid fuels. Participants also examined the future of sugar, bio-refineries, biofuels and allied value chains. A CEOs Leadership Summit brought policymakers and senior industry executives together to discuss competitiveness, strategic direction and long-term growth opportunities.

ISMA President Niraj Shirgaokar said the sugar industry had evolved from a traditional commodity sector into an integrated bio-refinery ecosystem contributing to energy security, rural prosperity and sustainable growth. He called for policy support, technology adoption and stronger collaboration to accelerate this transformation.

Mr. Deepak Ballani, Director General, ISMA, said, “ISBC 2026 has highlighted the significant opportunities emerging beyond traditional sugar and ethanol production, from diversified bio-refineries and Sustainable Aviation Fuel to modernised agriculture and circular economy solutions.”

The conference also highlighted opportunities beyond conventional sugar and ethanol, including diversified biorefineries, Sustainable Aviation Fuel, modernised agriculture and circular-economy solutions. An accompanying industry Expo showcased sugar and bio-energy technologies, including Flex Fuel vehicles from Hero and Toyota.

The conference concluded with an emphasis on innovation, competitiveness and greater value creation across India's sugar and bio-energy ecosystem through sustained collaboration among government, industry and technology providers.

title: Who actually operates Amazon Air aircraft? The airlines behind Amazon's cargo fleet
description:
Amazon Air is an air freight service that moves packages between fulfilment centres and sorting hubs.
A number of companies operate the cargo aircraft for Amazon: Air Transport International One of the biggest operators of the Amazon Air network is Air Transport International (ATI).
It is part of the Air Transport Services Group (ATSG) and previously provided aircraft and crew to Amazon before Amazon Air launched.
ABX Air ABX Air is another Amazon Air carrier partner and is also part of ATSG.
Amazon’s current Amazon Air Cargo website lists ABX among its direct air carrier partners.
text:
An Amazon-branded cargo jet operated by 21 Air recently made headlines following a runway overrun at Miami International Airport. The incident on 6 September remains under investigation.

Yet it highlights a little-known aspect of Amazon’s air cargo network: although Amazon has access to a fleet of more than 100 aircraft, it doesn’t actually operate the flights.

Instead the aircraft are flown by a network of specialist cargo carriers that provide the pilots, maintenance, and the regulatory approvals needed to conduct the flights.

What is Amazon Air?

Amazon Air is an air freight service that moves packages between fulfilment centres and sorting hubs.

Amazon launched the operation in the US in 2016 on wet leases. Its first aircraft, a Boeing 767 known as Amazon One, took to the skies that year and the operation expanded rapidly.

By December 2018, 40 aircraft were flying in and out of more than 20 US airports, with Boeing 737 freighters added for shorter routes, and Boeing 767s for higher-capacity operations.

Amazon expanded internationally and by 2022, its global network had grown to over 100 aircraft. By 2024, Amazon Air was serving more than 70 destinations worldwide.

Today, Amazon Air Cargo says its network has more than 100 aircraft and 250 daily flights, operated by carrier partners. On its website it states, “Amazon is not an air carrier: we provide ACAR Services by contracting with air carriers that operate the aircraft.”

Who flies Amazon aircraft?

A number of companies operate the cargo aircraft for Amazon:

Air Transport International

One of the biggest operators of the Amazon Air network is Air Transport International (ATI). It is part of the Air Transport Services Group (ATSG) and previously provided aircraft and crew to Amazon before Amazon Air launched.

According to ATSG’s 2024 SEC filing, at the end of 2024 ATSG was leasing 30 Boeing 767 freighters to Amazon and operating 21 Boeing 767s provided by Amazon.

ABX Air

ABX Air is another Amazon Air carrier partner and is also part of ATSG. Amazon’s current Amazon Air Cargo website lists ABX among its direct air carrier partners.

Sun Country Airlines

Another major Amazon Air operator is Sun Country Airlines. The Minneapolis-based passenger and cargo airline has operated Amazon cargo flights since 2020.

On its website, Sun County Airlines says its cargo operation flies 20 Amazon-owned freighters.

21 Air

Fleet data from industry experts Cirium shows 21 Air operating eight aircraft for Amazon.

The operator has been in the headlines following the runway overrun at Miami Airport on 6 September. The Amazon Air cargo jet involved was operated by 21 Air.

The National Transportation Safety Board is currently investigating the incident and no cause has been given.

Hawaiian Airlines

Amazon also uses Hawaiian Airlines to operate its largest freighters: Airbus A330-300 converted freighters.

Amazon announced the deal in 2022, saying Hawaiian would maintain and operate an initial fleet of 10 aircraft on Amazon’s behalf.

Despite Hawaiian’s acquisition by Alaska Air Group, the operation continues under Hawaiian.

ASL Airlines Ireland

In Europe, Amazon uses ASL Airlines Ireland. This is part of ASL Aviation Holdings.

ASL says it operates freight aircraft for companies and online retailers including Amazon, DHL and FedEx.

QuikJet

In India, Amazon Air operates through QuikJet Airlines. The Indian cargo carrier is part of the ASL Aviation group.

Amazon launched its dedicated air cargo operation in India in 2023.

Cargojet

Amazon has used Canada’s Cargojet to operate Amazon-owned Boeing 767 freighters.

How many aircraft does Amazon Air have?

Amazon Air says its network includes more than 100 aircraft globally.

Does Amazon own any of the aircraft?

In January 2021, Amazon announced its first purchase of aircraft, buying 11 Boeing 767-300s from Delta Air Lines and WestJet.

It also leases a significant number of aircraft.

Why doesn’t Amazon operate its own cargo jets?

Running an airline involves a lot more than just owning aircraft. It requires pilots, maintenance teams and extensive operational infrastructure.

Instead of building and managing all that itself, Amazon contracts specialist airlines that already have those systems, personnel and regulatory approvals in place.

Who is responsible for flight safety?

The flight preparation and operational safety decisions are made by the air carrier, rather than Amazon.

On its website, Amazon says, “The air carrier’s pilot-in-command has full authority over preparation and acceptance of cargo for transport on the aircraft and all other aspects of flight safety.”

Air carriers must follow FAA rules, including preflight planning.

This means when an Amazon-branded aircraft is involved in an incident, investigations are typically conducted with the airline operating the flight, which holds the air operator certificate and conducts the flight operations.

title: Palm Oil Substitute Made From Greenhouse Gas Emissions - Intelligent Living
description:
Rainforest clearance for oil palm plantations has destroyed critical habitats and displaced endangered wildlife like orangutans and Sumatran rhinos.
Researchers have turned industrial greenhouse gases into a sustainable palm oil substitute.
The Palm Oil Paradox: A Global Need Versus Environmental Cost The world’s reliance on vegetable oils creates a dilemma for manufacturers and consumers alike.
Replacing palm oil with other crop oils would require far more agricultural land, driving even more deforestation and habitat destruction.
Programs like the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil set ecological standards, but tracing every drop through global supply chains remains difficult.
text:
For decades, palm oil has been a staple of modern manufacturing. It appears in roughly half of all packaged products sold in supermarkets today. You will find it in baked goods, chocolates, margarine, laundry detergents, and luxury cosmetics. Manufacturers prize it for its smooth texture, long shelf life, and versatility.

But its environmental cost is well documented. Rainforest clearance for oil palm plantations has destroyed critical habitats and displaced endangered wildlife like orangutans and Sumatran rhinos. Draining and burning ancient peatlands also release large stores of carbon dioxide back into the atmosphere.

Now, a scientific collaboration has found a radical way forward. Researchers have turned industrial greenhouse gases into a sustainable palm oil substitute. By capturing factory emissions before they reach the atmosphere, they are turning a global pollutant into a useful resource. The process needs no farmland at all, pointing to a future where everyday goods are made from the very gases driving climate change.

The Palm Oil Paradox: A Global Need Versus Environmental Cost

The world’s reliance on vegetable oils creates a dilemma for manufacturers and consumers alike. Palm oil is an exceptionally efficient crop. It yields between three and four tons of oil per hectare each year, roughly four to ten times more than soybean, sunflower, or coconut oil.

That efficiency creates a paradox. Replacing palm oil with other crop oils would require far more agricultural land, driving even more deforestation and habitat destruction.

Certified sustainable sourcing has struggled to keep pace with soaring demand. Programs like the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil set ecological standards, but tracing every drop through global supply chains remains difficult. There is simply not enough certified oil to supply the cosmetics, food, and biofuel sectors, where crop-based biofuel demand has already pressured tropical forests.

This leaves industries with no easy agricultural way out. Innovators are looking beyond farming altogether, seeking ways to make fats without planting a single seed. One earlier effort even replaced palm oil with coffee grounds recovered from cafe waste streams. A workable palm oil substitute is no longer a luxury. It is a necessity for global climate targets.

A Two-Stage Bioprocess: From Industrial Exhaust to Camembert Yeasts

The breakthrough rests on a clever, two-stage fermentation process. It was developed by the Fraunhofer Institute for Interfacial Engineering and Biotechnology (IGB) in Straubing, Germany, with the US carbon recycling firm LanzaTech and the Swiss cosmetics maker Mibelle Group. The method needs neither fertile soil nor farming.

Stage 1: Gas Fermentation Turns Emissions Into Ethanol

LanzaTech uses specialized bacteria to turn carbon dioxide- and carbon monoxide-rich industrial exhaust gases into ethanol. At commercial sites such as steel mills, continuous bioreactors capture the gases billowing from the flues. The process resembles brewing beer, except captured greenhouse gases replace grain as the raw material. The bacteria feed on the emissions and produce pure ethanol.

Stage 2: Cheese Yeasts Turn Ethanol Into Fat

Fraunhofer’s oil yeasts then ferment that ethanol into a rich, palm oil-like fat blend. These yeasts are oleaginous, meaning they naturally store high amounts of fat inside their cells. Both stages rely only on naturally occurring, non-genetically modified microorganisms. The yeasts Fraunhofer uses are naturally found on cheeses like Camembert. Fed with ethanol, they convert the alcohol into a thick biological fat that closely mirrors the chemical profile of tropical oils.

This approach echoes other advances in carbon capture, such as work on CO2-consuming bacteria that turn industrial waste into useful chemical building blocks. In each case, heavy industry’s waste becomes a high-value commodity.

Cosmetics Validation: Laboratory Success to Skin Care Trials

Making an alternative fat is only half the battle. It must also meet strict cosmetic standards. The beauty industry needs ingredients with specific melting points, stability, and skin feel. Above all, manufacturers want a drop-in replacement that slots into existing formulas without a redesign. After successful trials at Fraunhofer IGB, the fat blend went through application testing at Mibelle Laboratories to confirm it met these criteria.

The results confirmed a versatile, high-quality, 100% palm oil-free fat with strong skin-care properties. Because it is natural and biologically derived, it blends easily into lotions, creams, and other personal care items without the synthetic feel of petroleum-based alternatives. Industry leaders see major supply-chain potential. Peter Müller, CEO of the Mibelle Group, noted that “this innovation is the result of our long-standing partnership with LanzaTech and a milestone for the cosmetics industry.”

Susanne Heldmaier, Head of Research and Technical Innovation at the Mibelle Group, added, “Following successful research in the laboratory, we have now been able to start developing the pilot process… This will enable us to develop cosmetic products that not only protect our skin but also contribute to protecting the environment.” The tests show this palm oil substitute can compete on performance, paving the way for everyday products that are genuinely free from tropical deforestation.

Twice as Sustainable: Keeping Carbon in the Loop

This palm oil alternative earns its environmental credentials through a circular lifecycle. Conventional crop farming runs on a linear model that constantly demands fresh land and water. Project lead Vanessa Wegat from Fraunhofer IGB puts it simply: using climate-harmful emissions as raw material makes the finished product “twice as sustainable.”

The dual benefit is easy to see. First, the process avoids rainforest clearing because no arable land is needed to grow the Camembert yeasts. There is no fertilizer runoff, no pesticide use, and no habitat destruction.

Second, it uses raw industrial emissions directly, keeping greenhouse gases out of the atmosphere. The approach fits a broader wave of companies converting CO2 emissions into everyday products, from laundry detergent made from carbon emissions to advanced materials like polypropylene made from captured waste CO2. The result is a functional palm oil substitute that acts as a carbon sink while it is being made.

Beyond Cosmetics: Opening a New Route for Sustainable Aviation Fuel

Cosmetics offer an immediate, high-margin market that can fund further development. But the implications reach far beyond beauty products. Aviation, in particular, is desperate for low-carbon fuels. LanzaTech says the breakthrough could open a new route to the HEFA (Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids) pathway for sustainable aviation fuel, commonly called SAF.

Conventional SAF leans on limited supplies of used cooking oil, animal fats, or dedicated oil crops that compete with food production, though researchers have also pursued other routes from CO2 to green fuel. Collecting waste oils is logistically complex and capped by local supply. Turning crops into jet fuel triggers the same land-use controversies as tropical farming.

By making fatty acids straight from captured industrial gases, fuel developers could gain a huge, scalable feedstock that bypasses land-use conflicts and supply bottlenecks. The route works much like the Alcohol-to-Jet concept, but it uses the biological fats produced by the yeasts. Continuous bioreactors could supply the sheer volume of sustainable raw material needed to decarbonize commercial flight.

Scale-Up at Leuna: Preparing for Kilogram-Scale Pilot Production

Moving from a lab beaker to commercial reality takes serious engineering. Making a palm oil substitute in a petri dish is a triumph; supplying global manufacturers requires industrial output. The project has therefore moved to kilogram-scale pilot production, scaled up step-by-step at the Fraunhofer Center for Chemical-Biotechnological Processes (CBP) in Leuna, a branch of Fraunhofer IGB.

The Leuna facility is renowned for scaling up biochemical engineering processes. At pilot scale, engineers must solve three core challenges before commercial production can begin:

Optimizing mass transfer so yeast cultures receive a steady, uniform supply of ethanol as the bioreactors grow from liters to cubic meters.

Managing the heat generated by fermentation in large vats, since yeast productivity drops sharply if temperatures drift.

Maintaining continuous culture health over long production runs, keeping the non-GMO yeasts lipid-rich batch after batch.

The scaling economics are highly promising because the feedstock, primarily carbon waste, is incredibly cheap and abundant.

The joint announcement, detailed in their September 2025 press release, began an intensive scaling phase. As the technology matures, production costs should fall, letting the synthetic fat compete on price with cheap tropical oils. Fraunhofer’s 2026 research feature continues to highlight how greenhouse gases yield a palm oil alternative that meets industrial demand without ecological compromise. The path from pilot plants to commercial refineries should accelerate as global rules for sustainable ingredients tighten.

Comparing Sustainable Alternatives

To understand how this emissions-to-fat technology stacks up against traditional options, researchers and industry analysts look at several key metrics:

Feedstock / Method Land Use Deforestation Risk Scalability Regulatory Path Conventional Palm Oil High (Agricultural) High Limited by arable land Established Alternative Vegetable Oils Very High Moderate to High Constrained by crop yields Established Emissions-to-Fat Fermentation Negligible (Industrial footprint) None High (tied to industrial output) Emerging / Pilot phase

Conclusion: A New Chapter for Circular Manufacturing

Making a palm oil substitute from greenhouse gases marks a major leap for green chemistry. By combining industrial carbon capture with natural microbial fermentation, scientists show that we do not have to choose between useful products and environmental protection. LanzaTech’s gas-to-ethanol expertise and Fraunhofer’s yeast conversion together provide a blueprint for the future.

As pilot production scales up in Leuna, this technology points to a future where cosmetics, household items, and clean aviation fuels are made from yesterday’s pollution. Closing the carbon loop would ease the pressure on tropical rainforests. Turning waste into a global commodity shows that human ingenuity can solve the ecological crises it created. Manufacturers may soon have a true, drop-in alternative that protects biodiversity, captures carbon, and delivers quality to consumers worldwide.

title: Southwest leads new push for low-cost airline lounges - Aerospace Global News
description:
Airport lounges have long been associated with first class, business class and the world’s premier full-service airlines.
Southwest lounges will be closely tied to Chase Southwest is developing the lounges in partnership with Chase.
A new premium Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card issued by Chase will launch in 2027 and include access to the lounge network.
Southwest has not yet disclosed the card’s annual fee, guest policy or whether other passengers will be able to buy lounge access.
IndiGo ties lounge access to its loyalty programme and co-branded cards, while AirAsia X bundles third‑party lounge access with its premium onboard product.
text:
Airport lounges have long been associated with first class, business class and the world’s premier full-service airlines. But some low-cost carriers have included lounges in their passenger experience, despite their lean operating models.

Southwest Airlines is the latest—and one of the most significant—examples.

The US carrier has announced its first airport lounge network, with initial locations at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport (AUS), Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI), Daniel K. Inouye International Airport in Honolulu (HNL) and Nashville International Airport (BNA).

Construction has already begun, with the first lounges expected to open from late 2027. Southwest says at least seven more locations will follow over the next several years.

The move is another striking departure from the traditional low-cost model the airline first perfected, and so many others followed over the decades. Southwest has recently left its long-successful model behind, introducing assigned seating, extra-legroom seats and baggage charges.

But Southwest is not alone. A number of low-cost airlines see premium airport services as another service element passengers may be willing to pay for—either directly, through ancillaries, through airline loyalty programmes or by signing up for revenue-generating airline credit cards.

Southwest lounges will be closely tied to Chase

Southwest is developing the lounges in partnership with Chase. A new premium Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card issued by Chase will launch in 2027 and include access to the lounge network. Southwest has not yet disclosed the card’s annual fee, guest policy or whether other passengers will be able to buy lounge access.

Chase operates its own expanding Sapphire Reserve Lounge Network. However, none of the first four airports Southwest has announced as lounge locations currently has a Chase Sapphire Lounge.

Chase currently lists Sapphire lounges at Boston, Dallas/Fort Worth, New York JFK, Las Vegas, New York LaGuardia, Philadelphia, Phoenix and San Diego, with Los Angeles coming soon. Its wider card benefits also include Priority Pass lounges and selected Air Canada Maple Leaf Lounges.

Southwest says its new lounges will combine its own hospitality with the “success of the Chase Sapphire Reserve Lounge Network,” including sophisticated design, locally inspired food and amenities similar to those found in Chase lounges today.

Neither Southwest nor Chase has yet said who will own and operate the facilities. For now, the four new facilities appear to be a distinct Southwest-branded lounge network developed with Chase rather than new Chase Sapphire Lounges.

Lounges require significant investment in real estate and service. Southwest could recover that investment through Chase card revenue and possibly by selling lounge passes as ancillaries.

JetBlue has already moved into the lounge business

Southwest is not the first US airline with low-cost roots to make the move. JetBlue opened its first BlueHouse lounge at New York JFK Terminal 5 in December 2025. The 9,000-square-foot, two-level facility includes food and drinks, high-speed WiFi, charging points, quiet areas and a game room.

Its second BlueHouse opened at Boston Logan Terminal C on 27 August 2026.

Eligible Mint passengers get complimentary access, as do top-tier Mosaic loyalty programme members and qualifying JetBlue credit card holders. JetBlue also sells limited access to some other eligible passengers.

The lounges encourage bookings of JetBlue’s Mint premium cabin product, sign-ups for the TrueBlue loyalty programme, and credit card business, while also generating ancillary revenue through access passes.

easyJet finds lounge partner at Gatwick

In 2021, easyJet opened The Gateway at London Gatwick’s North Terminal. Rather than build and operate a proprietary lounge, easyJet partnered with No1 Lounges to run the facility.

The Gateway offered hot and cold food, drinks, WiFi, charging facilities, work areas, a TV den and games room.

The airline closed the easyJet Gateway Lounge over two years ago, and returned the property to No 1 Lounges. It now offers Inclusive Plus fare paying passengers access to My Lounge at Gatwick’s North Terminal, which is a separate No 1 Lounges property.

The airline has partnered with lounge operators to offer their facilities at other airports as a benefit for its higher-fare-paying passengers.

easyJet’s Inclusive Plus fare offers up to three hours of lounge stays at select locations.

Birmingham Airport (BHX) – No1 Lounge

Bristol Airport (BRS) – Escape Lounge

Edinburgh Airport (EDI) – Escape Lounge

Jersey Airport (JER) – No1 Lounge

London Gatwick Airport (LGW) – My Lounge North Terminal

Luton Airport (LTN) – My Lounge

Manchester Airport (MAN) – Escape Lounge Terminal 2

Stansted Airport (STN) – Escape Lounge

In Milan, easyJet grants access up to two hours before flight boarding time:

Milan Malpensa Airport (MXP) – Alda Merini Lounge, T2

Milan Linate Airport (LIN) – Leonardo Exclusive Lounge

The airline also sells lounge access as an ancillary product.

Norwegian and Scoot choose asset-light alternative

Building a lounge is not the only way for a low-cost carrier to sell passengers a more premium airport experience.

Norwegian has adopted an especially asset-light model through its Norwegian Reward partnership with Lounge Pass.

Norwegian Reward members can pre-book access to more than 800 independent airport lounges at more than 250 airports worldwide. The airline currently advertises access from £14 and awards members CashPoints worth 8% of the lounge booking.

It gives Norwegian an attractive lounge offer for passengers, covering a large geographical area, without having to build, staff or operate a single lounge.

Singapore-based Scoot has also used third-party lounges rather than investing in its own facilities. It previously sold a product called Scoot-in-Style at Singapore Changi, which bundled priority check-in and boarding with access to the SATS Premier Lounge. Scoot treated the lounge much like other optional airport services. The airline later discontinued the ancillary product and now directs passengers to buy their own access passes to run terminal lounges independently.

Lounge access as an ancillary service is the easiest way to integrate lounges into the low-cost model. Airlines do not need to own or manage premium ground infrastructure. Instead, they can connect passengers to existing lounge operators and earn loyalty, ancillary revenue or both.

IndiGo links lounges to fares, loyalty and credit cards

IndiGo applies a variation on the easyJet model, with a Southwest spin. Like easyJet, India’s largest airline provides premium airport services delivered by partners rather than building a large proprietary lounge network. Like Southwest, IndiGo’s lounge access supports its loyalty programme and branded credit card.

Its BluChip loyalty programme has, for example, partnered with AirportZo, allowing members to earn five IndiGo BluChips for every ₹100 spent on services including airport lounges, meet-and-greet and porter services.

IndiGo is also connecting lounge access with its expanding co-branded credit card business.

The premium IndiGo SBI credit card currently includes up to eight domestic and six international lounge visits annually, subject to its terms and spending requirements. Its premium Axis Bank card offers eight domestic and two international visits annually.

flynas combines its own lounges with a partner network

Saudi Arabian low-cost carrier flynas has gone considerably further. Unlike Norwegian or IndiGo, flynas has put its own name on airport lounges while also using partnerships to extend lounge benefits much further across its network.

A flynas-branded lounge is available at Jeddah’s King Abdulaziz International Airport and Dammam’s King Fahd International Airport.

The airline has also developed lounge access as a loyalty benefit. In 2024, flynas signed an agreement with Saudi lounge operator Hayyak, giving Prime members of its nasmiles loyalty programme complimentary access to 18 Hayyak lounges around the country when travelling with flynas. Other flynas passengers could purchase access through the airline’s website or app.

At the time, flynas said the Hayyak partnership complemented three flynas lounges at Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam. Its current lounge listings show how the model has evolved, with Hayyak now listed at Riyadh while Jeddah and Dammam retain flynas-branded facilities.

Prime nasmiles members continue to receive complimentary Hayyak lounge access when flying with flynas, subject to the programme’s conditions.

The result is effectively a hybrid lounge strategy: invest in branded facilities at key hub airports while using a specialist lounge operator to provide a much broader lounge network.

For a low-cost airline, that offers many of the advantages of a traditional global airline lounge network without requiring the carrier to build lounges at multiple destinations.

AirAsia X includes lounges with its premium seats

AirAsia X provides another example of a low-cost carrier using someone else’s lounge infrastructure to strengthen its most expensive onboard product.

The long-haul low-cost airline includes three hours of complimentary Plaza Premium Lounge access with its Premium Flatbed product at participating departure airports.

AirAsia X can offer one of the traditional benefits of international Business Class—a pre-flight lounge—without operating the facilities itself.

Air Arabia sells lounge access as another extra

Air Arabia follows a similarly asset-light approach. Like Norwegian, the Middle Eastern low-cost airline offers airport lounge access as an additional airport service passengers can add to their journeys, alongside products such as fast track and meet-and-assist.

This turns the lounge into another optional ancillary: passengers who value it can pay for it, while customers seeking the lowest possible fare can opt out.

flydubai takes a hybrid model approach to lounges

flydubai sits towards the premium end of the low-cost spectrum. Like JetBlue, it is closer to a hybrid carrier model than a traditional low-cost model. It opened its own dedicated Business Class Lounge at Dubai International Terminal 2 in December 2024.

Passengers travelling from Terminal 3 can instead use Emirates’ Business Class Lounge, while flydubai also provides access to partner lounges at numerous overseas destinations.

Lounges can make sense for low-cost airlines

JetBlue and flydubai invest in their own lounges. easyJet has branded a lounge built by a specialist company. flynas blends branded lounges with a broader partner network. Norwegian and Scoot use an asset-light approach, connecting passengers to independent lounge operators. IndiGo ties lounge access to its loyalty programme and co-branded cards, while AirAsia X bundles third‑party lounge access with its premium onboard product.

These strategies let low-cost airlines target passengers willing to spend more while keeping travel affordable for everyone else.

A lounge can create another paid ancillary, strengthen a premium fare bundle, reward high-value frequent flyers and make a co-branded credit card considerably more attractive.

Airline loyalty programmes and credit-card partnerships have become major businesses in their own right.

Southwest’s new lounges are explicitly tied to a new Chase credit card rather than a new business class cabin. The airline can sell the basic seat relatively cheaply, and customers willing to spend more can improve the journey with an upgraded airport wait.

Southwest’s latest announcement also shows how far low-cost segmentation can go. An airline built around a famously simple passenger proposition will soon have assigned seats, extra-legroom sections, multiple fare bundles and its own airport lounges.

title: Satreskrim Polsek Plaju Tangkap Terduga Pelaku Pembunuhan Nenek dalam Waktu 50 Menit
description:
Menerima laporan, Kapolsek Plaju AKP Sutioso, S.H., M.H., M.Si.
bersama Kanit Reskrim Polsek Plaju Ipda Feby Julian Pratama, S.H., M.M., beserta tim opsnal, pawas dan piket fungsi langsung mendatangi lokasi untuk melakukan olah tempat kejadian perkara.

Sonny Mahar Budi Adityawan, S.I.K., M.H.
Nandang Mu’min Wijaya, S.I.K., M.H.
text:
INDODAILY.CO, PALEMBANG, —- Polda Sumatera Selatan melalui jajaran Polrestabes Palembang bergerak cepat mengungkap kasus dugaan pembunuhan terhadap perempuan lanjut usia berinisial K (66) di Jalan Kapten Robani Kadir, Kelurahan Talang Putri, Kecamatan Plaju, Kota Palembang, Sabtu dini hari (12/9/2026).

Polisi menangkap AS (23), yang merupakan cucu kandung korban, sekitar 50 menit setelah peristiwa tersebut dilaporkan.

Peristiwa itu terungkap setelah warga sekitar mendengar teriakan korban meminta pertolongan sekitar pukul 00.45 WIB. Saksi kemudian menghubungi ketua RT dan keluarga korban sebelum bersama-sama mendatangi rumah korban.

Setelah berhasil masuk ke dalam rumah, saksi bersama anggota keluarga mendapati korban tergeletak di lantai dalam kondisi bersimbah darah. Warga kemudian melaporkan kejadian tersebut kepada pihak kepolisian.

Menerima laporan, Kapolsek Plaju AKP Sutioso, S.H., M.H., M.Si. bersama Kanit Reskrim Polsek Plaju Ipda Feby Julian Pratama, S.H., M.M., beserta tim opsnal, pawas dan piket fungsi langsung mendatangi lokasi untuk melakukan olah tempat kejadian perkara.

Petugas kemudian berkoordinasi dengan piket reskrim dan Unit Identifikasi Polrestabes Palembang. Korban selanjutnya dievakuasi ke Rumah Sakit Bhayangkara untuk menjalani pemeriksaan visum et repertum.

Dari informasi masyarakat, polisi memperoleh petunjuk mengenai keberadaan AS yang diduga melarikan diri setelah kejadian. Tim Unit Reskrim Polsek Plaju yang dipimpin langsung Kapolsek dan Kanit Reskrim kemudian bergerak menuju lokasi persembunyian pelaku.

Sekitar pukul 01.35 WIB, polisi berhasil menangkap AS tanpa perlawanan berarti. Petugas selanjutnya membawa AS ke Polsek Plaju untuk menjalani pemeriksaan dan proses hukum lebih lanjut.

Dalam pengungkapan tersebut, polisi turut mengamankan sejumlah barang bukti, yakni satu pisau bergagang kayu berwarna cokelat dengan ukuran kurang lebih 10 sentimeter, satu pisau bergagang warna putih-hitam dengan ukuran kurang lebih 10 sentimeter, serta satu gunting berwarna oranye.

Berdasarkan hasil pemeriksaan awal, korban mengalami luka pada bagian hidung, luka tusuk pada tangan kiri, serta luka lebam pada bagian wajah. Penyidik masih melakukan pendalaman terhadap rangkaian peristiwa tersebut.

Atas dugaan perbuatannya, AS dijerat Pasal 458 Kitab Undang-Undang Hukum Pidana (KUHP) terkait tindak pidana pembunuhan. Proses penyidikan terus dilakukan untuk memastikan seluruh fakta dan rangkaian kejadian terungkap secara terang.

Kapolrestabes Palembang Kombes Pol. Sonny Mahar Budi Adityawan, S.I.K., M.H. mengapresiasi respons cepat personel di lapangan serta peran masyarakat dalam memberikan informasi kepada kepolisian.

“Kami mengapresiasi kecepatan respons anggota di lapangan serta partisipasi aktif masyarakat sehingga pelaku dapat diamankan dalam waktu singkat, dan kami pastikan proses hukum berjalan tuntas untuk memberikan rasa keadilan,” ujar Sonny.

Kabid Humas Polda Sumatera Selatan Kombes Pol. Nandang Mu’min Wijaya, S.I.K., M.H. menegaskan bahwa kepolisian akan terus mengambil tindakan tegas terhadap setiap tindak pidana yang mengancam keselamatan masyarakat.

“Kami akan menindak tegas setiap bentuk kejahatan yang mengancam keselamatan jiwa masyarakat. Kami juga mengimbau seluruh warga untuk meningkatkan kepedulian terhadap lingkungan dan bersama-sama menjaga kamtibmas,” ujar Nandang.

Pengungkapan dalam waktu singkat tersebut menunjukkan respons cepat jajaran kepolisian dalam menangani tindak pidana serta memberikan perlindungan kepada masyarakat.

Kepolisian juga mengajak warga segera melaporkan setiap kejadian atau informasi yang berpotensi mengganggu keamanan dan ketertiban masyarakat.

text:
JAKARTA, 13 September 2026 – Selama 57 tahun beroperasi, PT Pertamina Trans Kontinental (PTK) telah berkembang menjadi penyedia layanan maritim terintegrasi. Semakin melangkah, PTK akan perkuat operational excellence dengan modernisasi, digitalisasi dan kapal penunjang ramah lingkungan (green supporting vessel).

PTK didirikan pada tahun 1969 sebagai Anak Usaha PT Pertamina (Persero) dengan nama PT Pertamina Tongkang sebagai jasa kapal pandu tunda. Hingga tahun 1991, perusahaan mendirikan beberapa anak usaha untuk mendukung layanan maritim. Pada tahun 2011, nama PT Pertamina Tongkang berubah menjadi PT Pertamina Trans Kontinental.

Hingga kini, pengembangan bisnis telah terintegrasi pada layanan penunjang kemaritiman, mencakup penyediaan dan operasional armada kapal penunjang (support vessel), pelabuhan (port operation), layanan maritim (marine service) dan pangkalan logistik pesisir (shorebase) di sejumlah wilayah strategis Indonesia.

“Ke depan, kami akan perkuat modernisasi, digitalisasi serta green supporting vessel. Ini adalah masa depan PTK,” ujar Direktur Utama PTK Harris Abdi Sembiring Meliala pada Sambutannya saat Syukuran HUT ke-57 PTK di Kantor PTK Jakarta, Rabu 9 September 2026.

Era kapal ramah lingkungan di PTK dimulai tahun 2019, melalui kapal Transko Rajawali yang merupakan kapal tunda (harbour tug) berbahan bakar ganda (dual-fuel) pertama di Indonesia. Berukuran panjang 34 meter, kapal ini menggunakan bahan bakar soalr dan liquefaction natural gas (LNG), sehingga lebih ramah lingkungan dan rendah emisi.

PTK juga memperluas penggunaan bahan bakar hijau pada kapal penunjang lainnya, utility boat dan crew boat. Salah satunya, pada 11 Juni 2026, PTK berhasil melakukan pemasangan Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Surya (PLTS) pada Kapal Oil Barge (OB) Patra 2303. Inovasi hijau ini diklaim mampu memangkas emisi hingga 79,2 ton CO2 per tahun, sekaligus menekan ketergantungan armada logistik laut terhadap konsumsi bahan bakar diesel (solar).

Selain memperluas penggunaan panel surya, PTK juga menyiapkan uji coba Battery Management System (BMS) pada kapal mulai 2027 sebagai bagian dari pengembangan teknologi pendukung green shipping.

Harris menambahkan, saat ini PTK memiliki 370 kapal milik dan menyewa sekitar 82 unit kapal lainnya. PTK berencana menambah kapal baru sebagai upaya peremajaan dan modernisasi, termasuk untuk kapal eksisting. Hal ini guna terus meningkatkan kemampuan operasional PTK, sekaligus layanan excellence bagi pelanggan.

“PTK menjaga kualitas layanan dengan peremajaan serta modernisasi aset-asetnya. Kemudian digitalisasi operasi, di mana saat ini PTK sudah memiliki 21 digitalisasi di seluruh fungsi kerja. Ke depan, aplikasi ini akan meningkat menjadi Artificial Intelligence (AI) sehinga dapat membantu manajemen dalam mengambil keputusan,” jelas Harris.

Harris berharap, rencana tersebut didukung oleh seluruh pihak termasuk Pemegang Saham, Manajemen, Perwira Pekerja PTK, serta stakeholder untuk mendukung upaya tersebut. Tidak hanya untuk memajukan PTK untuk terus berkembang, maju dan unggul, namun mendorong industri maritime Indonesia yang berkelanjutan.**

title: BRICS backs deeper civil aviation cooperation, Sustainable Aviation Fuel push
description:
New Delhi: Civil aviation, sustainable aviation fuels and international aviation governance have figured prominently in the BRICS New Delhi Declaration, with member countries calling for deeper cooperation in transport policy, investment, technology and capacity building.
A key aviation-related focus is the promotion of Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAF) and Low-Carbon Aviation Fuels to reduce carbon emissions from international aviation.
BRICS welcomed the BRICS Forum on Sustainable Aviation Fuels and a framework for cooperation and knowledge exchange on transport decarbonisation, with the declaration highlighting the potential to leverage the renewable-energy resources of member countries.
The leaders also addressed the governance of international civil aviation.
BRICS leaders reaffirmed their commitment to implementing the Paris Agreement and strengthening international cooperation on climate resilience and emissions reduction.
text:
New Delhi: Civil aviation, sustainable aviation fuels and international aviation governance have figured prominently in the BRICS New Delhi Declaration, with member countries calling for deeper cooperation in transport policy, investment, technology and capacity building.

The declaration on Saturday welcomed the outcomes of the BRICS Transport Ministers’ Meeting held in Nagpur and said the grouping would further promote transport dialogue, including in civil aviation, to meet stakeholder demand and strengthen the transport potential of BRICS countries. The leaders also stressed the development of sustainable and resilient transport infrastructure, recognising its importance to economic growth, connectivity and environmental sustainability.

A key aviation-related focus is the promotion of Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAF) and Low-Carbon Aviation Fuels to reduce carbon emissions from international aviation. BRICS welcomed the BRICS Forum on Sustainable Aviation Fuels and a framework for cooperation and knowledge exchange on transport decarbonisation, with the declaration highlighting the potential to leverage the renewable-energy resources of member countries.

The declaration also links aviation with wider efforts to build resilient transport infrastructure, including the application of circular-economy principles in the development and maintenance of transport infrastructure. It further welcomed the establishment of a BRICS Logistics Supply-Chain Cooperation Framework, which could have implications for the movement of air cargo and the wider integration of transport networks.

The leaders also addressed the governance of international civil aviation. The declaration welcomed the entry into force of the 2016 amendment to Article 50(a) of the Convention on International Civil Aviation, which expands the membership of the ICAO Council by four seats to improve representation of underrepresented regions, including Africa and Asia-Pacific.

BRICS also welcomed the candidatures of Ethiopia, endorsed by the African Union as the sole African candidate, and Indonesia for the additional ICAO Council seats in elections scheduled during the 43rd (Extraordinary) ICAO Assembly.

The aviation provisions come against the broader backdrop of the declaration’s emphasis on climate action and sustainable development. BRICS leaders reaffirmed their commitment to implementing the Paris Agreement and strengthening international cooperation on climate resilience and emissions reduction.

text:
JAKARTA, INDODAILY.CO – PT Pertamina Patra Niaga melalui kapal tanker MT Mauhau turut membantu proses pencarian dan penyelamatan korban KMP Virgo Transport 08 yang dilaporkan tenggelam di perairan Laut Jawa, Minggu (13/9).

MT Mauhau yang tengah berlayar dari Banjarmasin menuju Tuban menerima informasi mengenai kejadian tersebut melalui radio VHF. Mengetahui adanya kapal yang tenggelam di sekitar wilayah pelayarannya, nakhoda dan awak kapal MT Mauhau segera melakukan respons dengan mendatangi lokasi dan membantu proses evakuasi korban.

Hingga laporan terakhir, sebanyak 16 orang berhasil dievakuasi ke atas MT Mauhau, termasuk nakhoda KMP Virgo Transport 08. Salah satu korban dilaporkan mengalami luka pada bagian kaki dan saat ini mendapatkan penanganan dari awak kapal MT Mauhau.

VP Corporate Communication PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Kitty Andhora menyampaikan bahwa aksi penyelamatan tersebut merupakan bentuk profesionalisme, kepedulian dan komitmen insan Pertamina untuk mengutamakan keselamatan serta membantu sesama, khususnya dalam situasi darurat di wilayah operasi dan pelayaran.

“Begitu menerima informasi adanya kapal yang tenggelam, Nakhoda dan crew MT Mauhau segera mengambil langkah untuk membantu proses penyelamatan. Keselamatan jiwa menjadi prioritas utama, dan kami bersyukur hingga saat ini 16 korban telah berhasil dievakuasi ke atas kapal,” ujar Kitty.

Dalam prosesnya, MT Mauhau juga telah berkoordinasi dengan Basarnas Banjarmasin. Tim Basarnas saat ini bergerak menuju lokasi kejadian untuk melanjutkan proses pencarian dan evakuasi. Sejumlah kapal lain, termasuk TB TCP 205 dan KMP Haidar, juga turut membantu proses penyelamatan.

Kitty menambahkan, Pertamina Patra Niaga terus berkoordinasi dengan pihak terkait dan memantau perkembangan proses evakuasi. Awak MT Mauhau juga memastikan para korban yang telah diselamatkan mendapatkan penanganan awal berupa makanan, minuman, serta bantuan sesuai kebutuhan selama menunggu proses evakuasi berikutnya.

“Kami terus berkoordinasi dengan Basarnas dan seluruh pihak yang terlibat. Fokus kami saat ini adalah memastikan para korban yang telah dievakuasi mendapatkan penanganan dengan baik dan mendukung proses pencarian terhadap korban lainnya,” ucap Kitty.

MT Mauhau merupakan kapal milik Pertamina Patra Niaga yang pada saat kejadian sedang dalam perjalanan menuju Tuban.

Sebagai bagian dari komitmen terhadap keselamatan pelayaran dan kepedulian sosial, Pertamina Patra Niaga senantiasa mendorong seluruh awak kapal dan pekerja untuk memberikan respons terbaik ketika menghadapi kondisi darurat di laut.
